title: E1: Build ChromaDB Vector Database for Career Knowledge
description: Set up and populate a ChromaDB vector database with rich metadata for semantic search across career history, projects, and life experiences. Target: filtered semantic search with metadata tagging (company, role, project, date range, type, confidence, source).

title: F1.7: Alt Questions as Separate ChromaDB Documents
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #8): Alt questions currently stored in tags field as comma-separated strings. ChromaDB dollar-sign-contains filter is keyword-only (substring match) — not semantic. So query 'how fast did the system become' will NOT match tag 'data freshness improvement'. The entire alt-question recall strategy is broken.

FIX: Store each alt question as a separate ChromaDB document with its own embedding.

STRUCTURE:
  Primary doc:
    id: career_project_20240308_cgb-latency_a3f2
    text: 'What was the data latency improvement in the CGB project?'  (primary Q + A)
    metadata: {type: qa_pair, primary_doc: true, ...full metadata}

  Alt doc 1:
    id: career_project_20240308_cgb-latency_a3f2_alt1
    text: 'How fast did the CGB data pipeline become after optimization?'
    metadata: {type: alt_question, primary_doc_id: career_project_20240308_cgb-latency_a3f2,
               ...same metadata as primary, is_alt: true}

  Alt doc 2:
    id: career_project_20240308_cgb-latency_a3f2_alt2
    text: 'What was the impact of CGB ingestion layer on data freshness?'
    metadata: {type: alt_question, primary_doc_id: career_project_20240308_cgb-latency_a3f2,
               ...same metadata as primary, is_alt: true}

RETRIEVAL CHANGE:
  When retrieving, filter OUT alt_question docs from direct results:
    where={is_alt: False}  OR  where={type: qa_pair}
  BUT alt docs participate in similarity search → their match elevates primary doc rank

  Alternatively: retrieve all (including alts), then deduplicate by primary_doc_id
  Show only primary doc, but rank boosted by alt question matches

RATIO: 1 primary doc + 2-3 alt docs per Q&A pair
  Increases ChromaDB document count by 3x — acceptable for personal-scale use

TAGS FIELD: Keep for categorical filtering (project names, domain tags, people names)
  Remove alt questions from tags entirely once this is implemented

title: F1.6: Required Metadata Fields Expansion for Career Documents
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #7): Schema has 7 required fields: domain, subdomain, type, importance, privacy, source, schema_version. But company, project, date_start — the most commonly used filter fields — are optional. Compound filters fail when these are null. Example: filter by company=sprinklr AND type=metric AND importance>=4 → zero results if company is null on any doc.

FIX: Domain-conditional required fields. Add 3 more required fields for career-domain documents.

REQUIRED FIELDS BY DOMAIN:

For domain=career (10 required fields):
  Base 7: domain, subdomain, type, importance, privacy, source, schema_version
  + company       (e.g., sprinklr, amex)
  + project       (e.g., cgb, crr_aml)
  + date_start    (e.g., 2022-04)

For domain=finance (9 required fields):
  Base 7 + date_start + currency

For domain=health (8 required fields):
  Base 7 + date

For domain=relationships (8 required fields):
  Base 7 + people

For all other domains: base 7 only

VALIDATION AT INSERT TIME:
  def validate_required_fields(pair: QAPair) -> ValidationResult:
    required = BASE_REQUIRED_FIELDS + DOMAIN_REQUIRED_FIELDS[pair.domain]
    missing = [f for f in required if pair.metadata.get(f) is None]
    if missing:
      return ValidationResult(valid=False, missing_fields=missing)
      # Block insert, prompt user: 'Yeh fields missing hain: [company, project]'
    return ValidationResult(valid=True)

MIGRATION:
  Existing documents without company/project → batch update job
  Query: collection.get(where={domain: career, company: null})
  For each: LLM infers company/project from document text
  Update with inferred values + flag confidence as 'inferred'

title: F1.5: Groundedness Threshold Calibration Protocol
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #6): Groundedness thresholds (G > 0.85 = high, 0.70-0.85 = medium, 0.50-0.70 = low, <= 0.50 = no match) are arbitrarily chosen. Different embedding models have completely different cosine similarity distributions. Threshold valid for text-embedding-ada-002 may be completely wrong for all-MiniLM-L6-v2.

FIX: Empirical calibration protocol to be run once after choosing embedding model.

CALIBRATION PROCEDURE:

Step 1 - Prepare test set (one-time, manual):
  20 POSITIVE pairs: (query, stored_doc) that ARE about same thing
    e.g., ('What was CGB latency improvement?', [the latency metric doc])
  20 NEGATIVE pairs: (query, stored_doc) that are NOT related
    e.g., ('What was CGB latency improvement?', [a Sprinklr salary doc])

Step 2 - Measure actual similarity scores:
  For all 40 pairs, compute cosine_sim(embed(query), embed(doc))
  Record score distribution for both positive and negative groups

Step 3 - Set thresholds at natural boundaries:
  HIGH threshold = 5th percentile of positive scores
    (95% of true matches will exceed this)
  NO-MATCH threshold = 95th percentile of negative scores
    (95% of non-matches will fall below this)
  MEDIUM and LOW = linear interpolation between the two

Step 4 - Document in config:
  GROUNDEDNESS_THRESHOLDS = {
    'model': 'text-embedding-3-small',
    'high': 0.87,       (example - actual values from calibration)
    'medium': 0.74,
    'low': 0.58,
    'no_match': 0.48,
    'calibrated_on': '2024-03-08',
    'test_set_size': 40
  }

Step 5 - Re-calibrate when: switching embedding model, or after 5000+ new documents added

NOTE: Translation layer (F0.6, F0.7) must be complete before calibration — thresholds are language-specific.

title: F4.12: Living Persona Disclaimer and Fictional Name Option
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #10): System simulates real living people (Elon Musk, Warren Buffett, Sadhguru). If a user screenshots 'Warren Buffett told me to invest in X' and shares it, this is misleading and potentially defamatory. Financial/health advice attributed to real famous people is a legal and ethical risk.

FIX - Two-part mitigation:

PART 1: Mandatory disclaimer footer on every expert response:
  Format: --- [italic small text]
  '*[Warren] yahan ek AI-inspired persona hai inspired by Warren Buffett ke philosophy.
  Yeh real Warren Buffett ki advice nahi hai.*'

  For finance/legal/health/investment topics, add additional line:
  '*Yeh educational simulation hai. Koi bhi financial/medical/legal decision ke liye
  qualified professional se milein.*'

  Disclaimer should be visually distinct (italic or smaller) — present but unobtrusive

PART 2: Fictional inspired names option (user-configurable, default: real names):
  Setting: persona_names = real | inspired
  If 'inspired':
    Warren Buffett → 'Valor' (value investor archetype)
    Elon Musk → 'Blaze' (moonshot entrepreneur)
    Esther Perel → 'Maya' (relationship wisdom)
    APJ Kalam → 'Kiran' (inspiring leader)
    Sadhguru → 'Siddha' (yogi wisdom)
  Each fictional name has same personality profile but no direct attribution to real person
  Reduces legal exposure while preserving persona value

IMPLEMENTATION:
  Add persona_names setting to session config
  Disclaimer auto-appended to every expert response via response wrapper
  Cannot be disabled by user (privacy/legal protection is non-negotiable)

title: F4.11: Privacy Firewall Query Enforcement
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #4): expert_data_access dict in readme defines which domains each expert can access, but this is just documentation. No actual enforcement exists at query time. If code calls collection.query() directly (bypassing wrapper), Warren could see relationship data.

FIX: Mandatory query wrapper — no raw collection.query() calls in expert-facing code.

IMPLEMENTATION:

def query_for_expert(expert_name: str, query_text: str, n_results: int = 5):
    allowed_domains = EXPERT_DATA_ACCESS[expert_name]
    return collection.query(
        query_texts=[query_text],
        where={'domain': {'in': allowed_domains}},
        n_results=n_results
    )

EXPERT_DATA_ACCESS map (enforced at runtime):
  satya_nadella:   [career, leadership]
  warren_buffett:  [finance, career_compensation]
  esther_perel:    [relationships, personal_growth]
  apj_kalam:       [career, identity, goals]
  sadhguru:        [health, personal_growth, beliefs]
  naval_ravikant:  [career, personal_growth, creativity]
  brene_brown:     [relationships, health, personal_growth]
  andrew_huberman: [health]
  charlie_munger:  [finance, decisions]
  elon_musk:       [career, goals]

SYSTEM CONTEXT retrieval (non-expert queries like conflict check, staleness):
  Use query_for_system(query_text, domain_filter) which bypasses expert restrictions
  But NEVER expose this to the expert's response generation

VALIDATION:
  Unit test: query_for_expert('warren_buffett', 'girlfriend fight', 5)
  Expected: 0 results (relationship data filtered out)
  Any result → privacy violation → block deploy

title: F0.8: Structural CE Validation (Replace LLM Absence Reasoning)
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #3): CE check currently asks LLM 'what information from raw answer is not in the pairs?' LLMs are provably unreliable at reasoning about absence - they miss what they don't explicitly see. For example: 'Maine CGB mein ingestion layer banaya, 14 APIs, 6 months lagi, 5 log the, latency 48h to 15min' - LLM extraction produces 4 pairs but misses '6 months duration' and '5-person team' because the LLM doesn't notice the gap.

FIX: Replace LLM-based CE check with mechanical structural extraction.

ALGORITHM:
  Step 1 - Extract all content atoms from English translation using NLP:
    - All numbers and units: 14, 48h, 15min, 6 months, 5 people, 78%
    - All named entities: CGB, Sprinklr, API, ingestion layer
    - All measurable attributes: latency, resolution rate, team size, duration
    - All actions: integrate, reduce, build, deploy

  Step 2 - For each extracted atom, check: does at least one Q&A pair's answer contain this atom?
    - Number 14 → found in pair [cgb-002] answer ✓
    - '6 months' → NOT found in any pair → GAP DETECTED
    - '5 people' → NOT found in any pair → GAP DETECTED

  Step 3 - For each gap, create new Q&A pair:
    Gap: '6 months duration'
    Auto-generated Q: 'How long did the CGB ingestion layer integration take?'
    Auto-generated A: 'The CGB unified ingestion layer integration took 6 months to complete.'

  Step 4 - Run ME check on new pairs to ensure no overlap with existing pairs

IMPLEMENTATION:
  Use regex + simple NLP (spaCy or similar) for atom extraction
  No LLM judgment required for Step 1-2 (purely mechanical)
  LLM only for Step 3 (Q generation from gap) - much narrower task, reliable
  
RESULT: Coverage is mathematically verifiable. Every number, entity, and measurable attribute from raw answer guaranteed to appear in at least one pair.

title: F5.7: Entity-Scoped Conflict Detection
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #2): 'VP of Product at Sprinklr (company: sprinklr)' and 'VP of Product at AmEx (company: amex)' have near-identical text. Current conflict check compares only text similarity → conflict_score is HIGH → system wrongly blocks a valid second entry.

FIX — Add entity scope filter to conflict_check query:

Before comparing any pair, check if new_pair and candidate share the SAME entity scope:
  Entity scope = {company, project} — defined by metadata, not text

Query change:
  CURRENT (wrong):
    collection.query(query_texts=[new_pair.text], n_results=5)

  FIXED (correct):
    collection.query(
      query_texts=[new_pair.text],
      n_results=10,
      where={'company': new_pair.metadata.company,
             'project': new_pair.metadata.project}
    )
  If company/project is empty → fall back to domain-scoped query

EXAMPLE:
  new: 'VP of Product' {company: amex, project: crr_aml}
  candidate: 'VP of Product' {company: sprinklr, project: cgb}
  → where clause filters OUT sprinklr candidate
  → No conflict found → safe insert ✓

EDGE CASES:
  - Fact about self identity (not project-specific): use domain=career, company=null → compare against all career facts
  - Cross-company fact: 'Both at Sprinklr and AmEx, I reported to VPs' → add to tags, not entity-scoped

ALSO HANDLES: Same person with same role across different teams within same company (project scope differentiates them)

title: F5.6: Temporal-Scoped Conflict Detection
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #1): 'Salary ₹15L in 2022' vs 'Salary ₹28L in 2024' triggers a conflict. But this is a valid career progression — NOT a contradiction. The current formula blindly compares text similarity without checking if the facts refer to the same time period.

FIX — Add temporal scope check BEFORE calculating conflict_score:

Step 1: Extract date metadata from both new_pair and candidate_pair.
Step 2: Check temporal overlap:
  - If existing.date_end < new.date_start → timeline update, no conflict
    Action: Link the two docs via related_id, update existing status to 'superseded'
  - If dates overlap OR both are undated → run full conflict check as normal
  - If new fact is undated and candidate is dated → warn user to add date context

FORMULA UPDATE:
  conflict_score = 0 if temporal_scope_check returns NO_OVERLAP
  conflict_score = Semantic_Sim × Contradiction_Magnitude if OVERLAP or UNDATED

EXAMPLES:
  'Salary ₹15L (2022-04)' vs 'Salary ₹28L (2024-07)' → NO_OVERLAP → safe insert, link as superseded
  'I am VP of Product (2023)' vs 'I am Senior Manager (2023)' → OVERLAP → conflict check

EDGE CASE: User says new fact without date. System should ask: 'Yeh kab ka hai? Date add karo taki main correctly handle kar sakun.'

title: F0.7: Hinglish-to-English Translation Layer (Query Side)
description:
When user searches or retrieves from ChromaDB in Hinglish, the query must also be translated to English BEFORE embedding and retrieval. This ensures the query embedding and stored document embeddings are in the same semantic space.

WHY BOTH SIDES NEED TRANSLATION:
If stored documents are in English but query is in Hinglish:
  Query: 'CGB mein latency ki problem kya thi?'
  Stored Q: 'What was the data latency challenge in the CGB project?'
  Without query translation: cosine_sim ≈ 0.45-0.55 (language mismatch)
  With query translation: cosine_sim ≈ 0.88-0.94 (language match)

HOW IT WORKS:
1. User types query in any language (Hinglish, Hindi, English)
2. Detect language (simple heuristic: if Devanagari chars OR Hindi words present → translate)
3. Translate to English using same LLM call
4. Embed translated query
5. Query ChromaDB with English embedding
6. Return results to user in their preferred language (Hinglish response)

QUERY TRANSLATION RULES (same as ingestion):
- Preserve technical terms: CRR, AML, APIs, OKR, etc.
- Preserve entity names unchanged
- Faithful translation, no semantic drift
- Examples:
  'CGB mein kya problem thi?' → 'What was the problem in the CGB project?'
  'Sprinklr mein salary kitni thi?' → 'What was the salary at Sprinklr?'
  'Kab leadership story capture kiya CGB ke liye?' → 'When was the leadership story captured for CGB?'

IMPORTANT:
- This is a lightweight operation — single LLM call before every query
- Cache translations of common queries to reduce latency
- User always sees response in Hinglish — only the internal retrieval uses English
- The system is invisible to user: they speak Hinglish, they get Hinglish answers, translation happens silently in between

title: F0.6: Hinglish-to-English Translation Layer (Ingestion Side)
description:
User conversation happens naturally in Hinglish, but ALL Q&A pair generation, embedding, and ChromaDB storage happens in full English.

WHAT THIS SOLVES:
- Embedding models (OpenAI ada-002, multilingual-e5, etc.) are trained predominantly on English. Hinglish text produces unreliable embeddings — same meaning in Hinglish vs English can get low cosine similarity, breaking conflict detection, retrieval, and MECE checks.
- With English-only storage, all similarity thresholds (0.75, 0.85, 0.50) become reliable and calibratable.

HOW IT WORKS:
1. User answers in Hinglish (e.g., 'CGB mein 14 APIs integrate kiye, latency 48h se 15min ho gayi')
2. Raw answer preserved VERBATIM in session file (source of truth stays in original language)
3. Before nugget extraction: translate full raw answer to English using LLM
4. All downstream steps (nugget ID, Q&A generation, metadata, embedding) use English translation

TRANSLATION RULES:
- Preserve technical terms as-is: CRR, AML, Sprinklr, AmEx, API, latency, OKR
- Preserve proper nouns: person names, city names, company names
- Preserve numbers and metrics exactly: '48h se 15min' → 'from 48 hours to 15 minutes' (no rounding)
- Preserve emotional tone: 'bahut frustrating tha' → 'was very frustrating' (not just 'challenging')
- Preserve tense and agency: 'Maine banaya' → 'I built' (not 'was built')

WHAT TO STORE:
- session file: raw Hinglish answer (verbatim, never modified)
- ChromaDB document text: English translation
- ChromaDB metadata tags: English keywords only
- Q question: English
- A answer: English

WHAT NOT TO DO:
- Do NOT translate project names, acronyms, technical jargon
- Do NOT summarize or paraphrase during translation — faithful translation only
- Do NOT lose numeric precision

title: F0.4: Q&A Pair Generator + Question Template Library
description:
Generate Q&A pairs from validated English nuggets. Both questions and answers must be in full English.

INPUT: List of validated, MECE English nuggets (from F0.2 + F0.3)
OUTPUT: Q&A pairs with primary question, 2-3 alt question phrasings, English answer

QUESTION GENERATION RULES:
- Primary Q: most likely how someone will search for this (English)
- Alt Q1: different angle — general vs specific
- Alt Q2: outcome/impact focused phrasing
- Alt Q3: 'why' or 'how' variant
- All questions in grammatically clean English

ANSWER RULES:
- Self-contained: reader needs no other document to understand it
- Start with entity context when ambiguous: 'At Sprinklr, during the CGB project...'
- Preserve exact numbers from nugget — no rounding
- 1-3 sentences, 100-1200 chars
- NEVER: 'as mentioned above', 'this refers to', 'see also'

QUESTION TEMPLATES BY ATOM TYPE:
  FACT:     'What was [X]?' / 'How did [Y] work?' / 'What was the architecture of [Z]?'
  STORY:    'Tell me about a time when [challenge]' / 'What happened when [scenario]?'
  METRIC:   'What was the [metric] for [project/role]?' / 'What was the impact of [X]?'
  DECISION: 'Why was [X] chosen over [Y]?' / 'What drove the decision to [Z]?'
  LESSON:   'What did you learn from [X]?' / 'What would you do differently about [Y]?'

ALT QUESTIONS STORAGE:
- Store alt questions in tags field (comma-separated)
- ALSO create 2-3 additional ChromaDB documents with alt question as text, same answer
- This gives each alt question its own embedding → much better recall
- All linked via related_id

title: F0.3: MECE Validation Algorithm
description: ME Check: cosine_sim(nugget_i, nugget_j) > 0.85 → merge. LLM semantic check for subtle overlaps. CE Check: LLM gap analysis — 'koi information from raw answer NOT in current pairs?' → create new pairs for gaps.

title: F0.2: Atomic Knowledge Extraction (Nuggets First)
description:
Algorithm to extract atomic knowledge units (nuggets) from user's raw answer.

INPUT: English translation of raw Hinglish answer (from F0.6 translation layer)
OUTPUT: List of nuggets, each with classified atom type

EXTRACTION RULES:
- 1 nugget = 1 subject + 1 predicate (one thing about one entity)
- Sentences with 2 distinct outcomes → 2 separate nuggets
- Every number/metric → always its own nugget (never merged with architectural facts)
- Pronoun references resolved to full entity before splitting ('it' → 'the CGB ingestion layer')
- Min 100 chars per nugget (merge with neighbor if smaller)
- Max 1500 chars per nugget (force semantic split if larger)

5 ATOM TYPES:
  FACT:     System description, how X works, process description
  STORY:    Sequence of events with outcome (STAR structure)
  METRIC:   Numbers, percentages, timelines, growth figures
  DECISION: 'chose X over Y', tradeoffs, why options were evaluated
  LESSON:   'learned', 'mistake', 'would do differently'

LLM PROMPT FORMAT:
'From this English text, extract ALL distinct knowledge atoms.
Rule: 1 atom = 1 standalone fact readable without other context.
Rule: Every number is a separate atom.
Output: numbered list only, no explanation.'

NOTE: All nugget text is in English. Technical terms preserved as-is (CRR, API, OKR).

description: Implement: Groundedness = max(cosine_sim) over retrieved docs. Decision: >0.85 cite source, 0.70-0.85 caveat, 0.50-0.70 flag uncertainty, ≤0.50 deny and ask user to provide info. Synthesis limit: max 3 vectors per output with citations.

title: F5.1: Conflict Detection Algorithm
description: Implement: Conflict Score = Semantic_Similarity × Contradiction_Magnitude. Thresholds: >0.6 hard block, 0.3-0.6 warn, 0.1-0.3 enrichment, <0.1 safe. Different contradiction magnitude formulas for METRIC, FACT, DATE, STORY atom types.

title: F4.15: Conversational Framing for Emotional Use Cases
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #13): One-by-one numbered question flow ('Q3 of 7: Tumhe kaisa laga?') feels clinical and interrogative for relationship and health use cases. Esther Perel and Brene Brown would never conduct therapy with numbered questions and progress trackers.

FIX: Differentiate question delivery style by use case category.

TWO MODES:

STRUCTURED mode (career, finance, productivity use cases):
  - Numbered progress visible: 'Q3 of 8'
  - Direct questions: 'Biggest achievement in last 12 months? Numbers ke saath.'
  - Explicit transitions: 'Theek hai, ab next topic...'
  - Time-boxed: user can see how many remain

CONVERSATIONAL mode (relationship, health/mental, personal growth, memories use cases):
  - NO question numbers, NO progress tracker
  - Questions disguised as curiosity/reactions: 'Aur... us moment mein andar kya hua?'
  - Transitions feel natural: 'Interesting. Aur is situation se pehle — kab se yeh pattern hai?'
  - Depth through follow-ups, not numbered questions
  - Expert signature phrases used naturally (Esther: 'Tell me more about what you wanted vs what happened')
  - Silence allowed: system doesn't rush to next question if user pauses

USE CASE MAPPING:
  STRUCTURED: C1-C12 (career), F1-F5 (finance), CR1-CR3 (creativity)
  CONVERSATIONAL: R1-R7 (relationships), H1-H6 (health), P3/P5 (journaling/identity), M1-M3 (memories)
  HYBRID: P1/P2/P4/P6 (goals/habits/learning — structured goal but empathetic tone)

IMPLEMENTATION:
  session_config.question_mode = STRUCTURED | CONVERSATIONAL | HYBRID
  Set based on use_case at session load
  CONVERSATIONAL mode disables: question counters, explicit transitions, time estimates
  Expert's conversational openers and depth_triggers replace structured question bank

title: F4.14: Session State Persistence in ChromaDB
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #12): Session state (last_question, answered[], pending[]) is designed in sync-life.md but never defined WHERE to persist it. If Claude session ends mid-way, all progress is lost. Also not queryable across devices.

FIX: Store session state as a ChromaDB document.

SCHEMA (document_record type):
  id: session_{use_case}_{date}_{hash}
  text: 'Session state for [use_case] started on [date] with expert [expert_name]. Progress: [N] of [M] questions answered.'
  metadata:
    type: document_record
    category: session_state
    domain: ai_meta
    privacy: private
    session_id: [unique id]
    use_case: C1
    expert: satya_nadella
    status: in_progress  (not_started / in_progress / paused / complete)
    last_question_index: 3
    total_questions: 8
    answered_indices: '1,2,3'   (comma-separated, ChromaDB needs scalars)
    pending_indices: '4,5,6,7,8'
    committed_pairs: 12
    pending_review: 2
    last_updated: '2024-03-08T14:30:00'
    raw_answers_file: 'career history/Sprinklr/CGB/Interview Sessions/session_20240308.md'

OPERATIONS:
  Create: at session start, upsert with status=in_progress
  Update: after each answer, upsert with updated answered_indices and last_question_index
  Resume: collection.get(where={category: session_state, use_case: C1, status: in_progress})
  Complete: update status=complete

RESUME PROMPT at session start:
  Check for in_progress sessions matching current use_case
  If found: 'Pichli baar hum [use_case] mein Q[N] pe ruke the. Continue karein?'
  If multiple in_progress: show list with dates, let user choose

title: F4.13: Multi-Expert Consensus Resolution Framework
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #11): When two experts disagree (e.g., Elon says 'quit and start up', Warren says 'never risk what you have'), the user is left with 'dono sun lo, tum decide karo.' This creates decision paralysis instead of empowerment.

FIX: Context-based resolution after expert disagreement.

DETECTION: After each expert responds in debate format, system checks:
  - Do the two responses recommend opposite actions?
  - If yes → trigger consensus resolution protocol

RESOLUTION FORMAT:
  System (neutral voice, not as any expert):
  'Dono valid hain — alag alag contexts ke liye.

  [Expert A] sahi hai agar: [condition that makes A's advice optimal]
  [Expert B] sahi hai agar: [condition that makes B's advice optimal]

  Tumhari situation mein: [follow-up question to identify which condition applies]'

EXAMPLE:
  Elon: 'Quit and build the startup.'
  Warren: 'Never risk what you have for what you don't have.'
  System: 'Dono sahi hain alag contexts ke liye.
    Elon sahi hai agar: tumhare paas 18+ months runway hai, co-founder hai, strong BATNA hai
    Warren sahi hai agar: runway 6 months se kam hai, family dependents hain, safety net weak hai
    Tumhara case kya hai — runway kitna hai abhi?'

This forces user to self-assess their context → they arrive at the right answer themselves.

FALLBACK: If system cannot determine context conditions (too ambiguous) → 'Dono ki ek-ek key insight note karo. Phir apne gut se decide karo — tumhara gut usually sahi hota hai.'

NEVER: 'I cannot advise which is better.' — that is a cop-out, not helpful.

title: F5.9: Staleness Detection and Auto-Expiry
description:
PROBLEM: Stored fact from 2022: 'My savings is 5 lakh.' In 2026 this is silently outdated. Truth engine never flags it because no new fact contradicts it. Silent staleness is more dangerous than a detected conflict.

FIX: Expiry-based staleness detection system.

STEP 1 - Domain-specific expiry config:
  finance (salary, savings): 365 days
  health (weight, fitness):  180 days
  career (role, company):    730 days
  relationships:             365 days
  identity/values:           1825 days
  memories/STAR stories:     never expire

STEP 2 - At insert time, compute expiry_date:
  expiry_date = date_of_fact + domain_expiry_duration
  Store in existing expiry_date metadata field (already in schema, currently unused)

STEP 3 - Weekly staleness check:
  stale = collection.get(where={'expiry_date': {'lt': today}})
  Add all stale docs to review_queue

STEP 4 - Review queue prompt at next session start:
  'Kuch purani information verify karni hai:
   - [2022] Salary 15L tha - kya ab bhi sahi hai?
   - [2022] Savings 5L thi - update karna chahoge?
   Options: [Still valid] [Update] [Delete]'

STEP 5 - User response handling:
  Still valid: reset expiry_date for another cycle
  Update: run conflict check on new value, store with new expiry
  Delete: mark status=archived (never hard delete - audit trail preserved)

title: F5.8: Expanded Conflict Candidate Pool at Scale
description:
PROBLEM (Stress Test #14): conflict_check queries only top 5 semantically similar documents (n_results=5). At 10,000+ documents, a conflicting fact at rank 6-10 is completely missed. Semantic similarity alone is not sufficient coverage for conflict detection.

FIX — Two-pass conflict search strategy:

PASS 1 (Semantic): Top 5 by cosine similarity (existing approach)
  → Catches conflicts with similar phrasing

PASS 2 (Structural): Targeted search by metadata filters — no n_results limit
  Filter: same {company, type, category} as new_pair
  → Catches conflicts with different phrasing but same structural position
  Examples of what Pass 2 catches that Pass 1 misses:
    'Data freshness improved 192x' (Pass 1 result) vs
    'Latency reduced from 48h to 15min' (same metric, different phrasing — found in Pass 2)

UNION both result sets → deduplicate by doc_id → run conflict_score on all

PERFORMANCE CONSIDERATION:
  Pass 2 uses metadata filter (fast indexed lookup in ChromaDB) not embedding search
  Only runs for METRIC and FACT atom types where structural conflicts are most common
  STORY, DECISION, LESSON types skip Pass 2 (conflicts are inherently phrasing-dependent)

RESULT:
  - METRIC conflicts caught even when phrased completely differently
  - FACT conflicts caught when stored under same company+category
  - No performance penalty for STORY/DECISION/LESSON types

title: F0.5: Metadata Auto-Assignment + Dynamic Extension
description: Inherited metadata (company, project, role, source) + per-pair metadata (type, category, importance, tags, related_id, emotion). 3-tier fallback for unknown fields: existing 47 → tags overflow → extra_metadata JSON. Auto-discovery loop every 50 pairs.

title: F5.5: Synthesis Limit + Attribution Format
description: Cap at 3 vectors per synthesized output. Each cited: (Source: doc_id, confidence: X.XX). If >3 vectors needed → ask narrower question instead of synthesizing. Attribution shown inline in responses.

title: F5.3: Change Log and Audit Trail
description: Every correction creates a document_record type entry with: old_doc_id, old_value, new_value, resolution, date, context. This enables full history of what changed and why. Never delete — only supersede.

title: F4.7: Session Continuity + State Tracking
description: Persist session state per use case: last_question, answered[], pending[]. Resume from last position. Show progress: Q3 of 8 answered. Allow mid-session pause and resume.

title: F4.6: Multi-Expert Panel System
description: Support 2-3 experts simultaneously. Sequential format (each responds in turn) and Debate format (adversarial perspectives). Privacy firewall: each expert sees only their domain data. Clear [Name]: labels in output.

title: F3.1: Create Interview Prep Templates
description: Build context/interview-prep/ with: behavioral question templates, STAR story checklist, technical question index, company research template, salary negotiation guide.

title: F3.2: Build Project Documentation Template
description: Create context/templates/ with: 15-question project analysis template, metrics tracking template, technical deep-dive outline, stakeholder analysis framework.

title: F2.3: Organize Reference Materials
description: Categorize and index all PDFs, Confluence exports, and documentation. Tag by: company, project, category (architecture, design, metrics, learning), date range. Create index file.

title: E3: Create context/ Directory for Reference Materials
description: Build READ-ONLY context directory with curated reference materials, templates, and guidelines for interview prep, project documentation, and knowledge organization.

title: F1.3: Create Search & Query Interface
description: Build interface (CLI or web) for filtered semantic search. Support queries like: 'Projects involving ML', 'Leadership examples at Sprinklr', 'Achievements in first 6 months'. Return ranked results with confidence scores and source metadata.

title: F1.4: Test & Validate Vector Quality
description: Write tests for search quality, metadata extraction accuracy, and ranking relevance. Test with known queries. Measure: precision, recall, MRR (mean reciprocal rank). Document findings.

title: F4.9: Accountability Partner Mode
description: Expert tracks user commitments from past sessions. Proactively follows up: 'Pichli session mein tumne kaha tha X karoge — kya hua?' Stores commitment as goal type with follow_up_status field.

title: F4.8: Small Talk Passive Capture
description: In small talk mode, detect factual claims, metrics, decisions, people, dates. Flag as confidence: 0.6. Surface with: 'Tumne kaha ki X — isko record karun?' Once per claim, never repeat. Weekly review queue.

title: F3.3: Create Knowledge Organization Guide
description: Write context/ORGANIZATION.md: naming conventions, tagging schema, metadata structure, search best practices, maintenance guidelines.
